expectations.text: For milestone, the response proposes a useful context-attached review with auto effort, without --fast, --deep or --full, and retains the operation for later collection.
expectations.evidence: A.md:5 proposes an 'auto-effort asynchronous checkpoint now' because independent work remains. The command at lines 9–11 attaches context and omits all three flags. Lines 100–106 require retaining the operation ID and collecting that same operation.

expectations.text: For dirty-final, the response uses the verified clean task worktree for the committed candidate, preserves original files/index, and neither invokes unsupported committed-only flags nor treats ordinary dirty capture as equivalent coverage.
expectations.evidence: A.md:22 selects the 'verified task-only clean worktree at the intended commit, not the original dirty worktree.' Lines 31–35 preserve original files/index, leave unrelated work untouched, reject invented committed-only flags and same-file path filtering, and explain that isolation establishes candidate scope.

expectations.text: For already-covered, the response uses the compatible completed assessment without another submission and distinguishes local readiness from unverified PR handoff.
expectations.evidence: A.md:39 says 'Reuse the completed assessment' with 'No review command or new context submission.' Line 41 reports 'ready locally' and explicitly excludes claims about hosted review, CI, merge or deployment.

expectations.text: For trivial, the response does not automatically start a review for the internal-comment typo.
expectations.evidence: A.md:45 says 'Do not submit an automatic review' for the behavior-neutral internal-comment typo; line 47 requires no command or context submission.

expectations.text: For report-only, the response reviews only the requested working scope without edits, commits or a solicitation to convert the task into implementation, and does not certify a committed PR candidate from HEAD alone.
expectations.evidence: A.md:51 selects the requested safe 'uncommitted working scope, without committing or editing.' Lines 58–62 prohibit PR preparation, fixes and solicitation to convert the request into implementation. It makes no HEAD-based committed-candidate certification; line 106 requires actual coverage inspection before readiness claims.

expectations.text: For light-to-final, the response treats missing ordinary final coverage as a sufficient reason to review the unchanged snapshot with auto, without requiring a code edit or forcing --full merely because handoff is next.
expectations.evidence: A.md:66 explicitly identifies 'missing ordinary final coverage' as the reason to proceed despite unchanged code and complete prior path coverage. Lines 69–79 propose auto review without --fast, --deep or --full and require checking actual final coverage rather than accepting light evidence alone.

expectations.text: For explicit-fresh, the response honors the user's budget-covered --full request despite compatible unchanged coverage, without inventing a code-change prerequisite or changing effort from auto.
expectations.evidence: A.md:83 honors the explicit within-budget request; line 86 includes --full. Line 89 retains auto effort, and line 93 explicitly acknowledges compatible coverage, settled findings and unchanged code while identifying the user's request as sufficient justification.

expectations.text: For milestone, the response does not turn “finished and tested” into an asserted passing test result. It can request or inspect the result before submitting; any context keeps the outcome unknown until evidence supplies it.
expectations.evidence: A.md:15 states 'Tests were run, but their outcome is not supplied.' Neither the milestone rationale nor its context asserts that tests passed.

claims.claim: The proposed commands use auto effort when neither --fast nor --deep is supplied.
claims.evidence: A.md:10,25,54,69 omit both flags. qodo-auto-help.txt:62–64 explicitly defines no depth flag as auto.

claims.claim: --full requests fresh assessment and does not itself imply deep effort.
claims.evidence: A.md:89 makes this distinction. qodo-auto-help.txt:19–20 defines --full as a fresh full review, while lines 25–26 separately define effort flags.

claims.claim: Asynchronous submissions return an operation ID that can be collected with qodo review status.
claims.evidence: A.md:100–104 proposes this collection procedure, consistent with qodo-auto-help.txt:29–36 and 66–68. This verifies CLI semantics, not an actual submission.

claims.claim: All commands are proposals rather than executed operations.
claims.evidence: A.md:1 explicitly says 'All commands below are proposals only,' consistent with task.md:6.

suggestions.reason: The assertions establish proposal-level correctness only. A separate controlled execution evaluation would be needed to verify context-file creation and delivery, actual capture boundaries, original files/index preservation, operation retention, and completed review coverage.

eval_feedback.overall: All eight assertions are supported by the proposal. No passing-test or completed-review outcome is invented. Context contents are partly outlines rather than created files; commands, filesystem preservation and review outcomes remain operationally unverified.

grader_provenance.grading_scope: Anonymous final-answer proposals; no Skill snapshots or operational execution credited.
